problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=-3.$ Given that the point $P(1,-3,8)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}+y\sqrt{x}$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$

feedback.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=2.$ Given that the point $P$ with $x$-coordinate $3$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}}}{y-x}$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point where $x=3$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(3,2).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(3,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(3,2) & =\frac{\sqrt{(3)^{2}-2(2)^{2}}}{2-3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{9-8}}{-1} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
